result.question: I'd rather take Transformer 1 at site MAIN out of service once than three times. Pull every open and pending-approval work order on it. For each one, give me the number, description, priority and scheduled date, and say whether it needs the unit de-energized, for example internal inspection, OLTC work or electrical testing, or whether it can be done live, for example oil sampling. Group the outage-needing work orders into bundles. Each bundle must have at least two work orders whose scheduled dates fall within 14 days of each other. For each bundle, propose a single outage date where the MAIN calendar has the fewest other scheduled work orders. Estimate each bundle's total planned hours, using the planned hours on the work orders themselves. Where a work order has no plan, use the average actual hours of closed work orders on Transformer 1. Then check the latest acetylene and hydrogen. If acetylene is above 1 ppm, any bundle with OLTC or inspection work moves to the earliest possible date regardless of calendar load. If fewer than two outage-needing work orders exist, don't bundle anything. Recommend whether each one should be done alone or deferred to the next planned outage, and why.
result.answer:
## Transformer 1 (MAIN) — Open / Pending-Approval Work Orders

Only **one** work order exists on Transformer 1 in any non-terminal status (WAPPR, APPR, INPRG, etc.). There are also **no closed/completed work orders** on this unit.

| WO # | Description | Priority | Status | Scheduled date | Outage needed? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1000051** | OLTC inspection – on-load tap changer (suspected contact wear/coking) | **1** (highest) | WAPPR (awaiting approval) | **None scheduled** (schedstart / targstart blank; long description references a target of 2024-01-19) | **Yes – de-energized.** OLTC internal inspection requires the unit isolated, earthed and the diverter/selector compartment drained. Cannot be done live. |

### Planned hours
- WO 1000051 carries **no plan** (`estlabhrs` null, no `wplabor` lines).
- Fallback rule (average actual hours of closed WOs on Transformer 1) **cannot be applied** – there are zero closed work orders on this asset, so no history exists.
- **Estimate: not determinable from records.** Engineering rule-of-thumb for an OLTC internal inspection with contact check/cleaning is on the order of 8–16 h plus oil handling, but that is not derived from the work-order data and should be confirmed by the planner.

### Latest DGA (last reading 2024-01-19 — data is ~2.7 years stale)
- **Acetylene (C₂H₂): 7 ppm** → **above the 1 ppm threshold**
- **Hydrogen (H₂): 2,850 ppm** → very high (typical IEC 60599 concern level ≈ 100–150 ppm)
- Combination is consistent with the WO note (T2 thermal fault / arcing, likely in the OLTC compartment or oil communication from it).

### Bundling
- **No bundles formed.** Only one outage-needing work order exists, which is below the minimum of two, and there is nothing else to co-schedule it with — including the live-work category (no oil-sampling, IR-scan or similar WOs are open).

### Recommendation for WO 1000051 — **Do it alone, do not defer**
- **Why not defer:** Acetylene is 7 ppm (> 1 ppm trigger) with H₂ at 2,850 ppm. Under your own rule, any OLTC/inspection work moves to the **earliest possible date regardless of calendar load**. Acetylene indicates arcing; combined with suspected contact coking, this is a progressive failure risk to the tap changer and possibly the main tank. Waiting for a "next planned outage" that has nothing else in it gains no efficiency and adds risk.
- **Calendar:** The MAIN calendar has **0 other scheduled work orders** for 2026-09-30 through 2026-10-31, so there is no conflict at any date. **Proposed outage date: the earliest date the crew and oil-handling resources can be mobilised — target 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-03.**
- **Actions to make the single outage worthwhile:**
  1. Approve WO 1000051 now (it is still WAPPR) and set `schedstart`.
  2. Add a fresh **live** DGA/oil sample **before** the outage — the last reading is from January 2024, so the true current gas trend is unknown; a new sample confirms urgency and may reveal whether gassing is confined to the OLTC compartment.
  3. Add as child tasks while the unit is already de-energized (so you don't come back later): winding-resistance / ratio test across taps, contact-resistance on the diverter, OLTC oil replacement, and bushing power-factor tests. These are outage-only tests that would otherwise force a second outage later.
  4. Assign a planned-hours estimate and technician (WO note flags that no technician has prior history on this unit).

**Caveats:** IoT data is stale (Jan 2024), the WO has no plan or schedule, and there is no closed-WO history for hour estimation — all three should be resolved before the outage is locked in.
